questions.text: The probability that a randomly chosen $2 \times 2$ matrix with all the entries from the set of first 10 primes, is singular, is equal to :

options.D:
$\frac{271}{10^{4}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. Let matrix A is singular then $|\mathrm{A}|=0$
Number of singular matrix = All entries are same + only two prime number are used in matrix
$$\begin{array}{l}
=10+10 \times 9 \times 2 \\
=190
\end{array}$$

Required probability $=\frac{190}{10^{4}}=\frac{19}{10^{3}}$

questions.text:
Let the solution curve of the differential equation $x \frac{d y}{d x}-y=\sqrt{y^{2}+16 x^{2}}, y(1)=3$ be $y=y(x)$.
Then $\mathrm{y}(2)$ is equal to :

options.D:
17

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{vx} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathrm{v}+\mathrm{x} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow x \frac{d v}{d x}=\sqrt{v^{2}+16} \\
\Rightarrow \int \frac{d v}{\sqrt{v^{2}+16}}=\int \frac{d x}{x} \\
\Rightarrow \ln \left|v+\sqrt{v^{2}+16}\right|=\ln x+\ln C \\
\Rightarrow y+\sqrt{y^{2}+16 x^{2}}=C x^{2} \\
\text { As } y(1)=3 \Rightarrow C=8 \\
\Rightarrow y(2)=15
\end{array}$$

questions.text: If the mirror image of the point (2, 4, 7) in the plane $3 \mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}+4 \mathrm{z}=2$ is (a, b, c), the $2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+2 \mathrm{c}$ is equal to :

options.D:
-42

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
sol. $\frac{\mathrm{a}-2}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{b}-4}{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{c}-7}{4}=\frac{-2(6-4+28-2)}{3^{2}+1^{2}+4^{2}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{-84}{13}+2, \mathrm{~b}=\frac{28}{13}+4, \mathrm{C}=\frac{-112}{13}+7 \\
\Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+2 \mathrm{c}=-6
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Let $\quad \vec{a}=\alpha \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-\hat{k}, \vec{b}=3 \hat{i}-\beta \hat{j}+4 \hat{k} \quad$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ where $\alpha, \beta \in \mathrm{R}$, be three vectors. If the projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{c}$ is $\frac{10}{3}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=-6 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+10 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$, then the value of $\alpha+\beta$ equal to :

options.D:
6

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}}{|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}|}=\frac{10}{3}$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\alpha+6+2}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}=\frac{10}{3} \Rightarrow \alpha=2$$
and $\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & -\beta & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & -2\end{array}\right|=-6 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow 2 \beta-8=-6 \Rightarrow \beta=1 \\
\Rightarrow \alpha+\beta=3
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}+(2 i- 1)=0$. Then, the value of $\left|\alpha^{8}+\beta^{8}\right|$ is equal to :

options.D:
1500

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $\mathrm{X}^{2}=1-2 \mathrm{i} \quad \Rightarrow \alpha^{2}=1-2 \mathrm{i}, \quad \beta^{2}=1-2 \mathrm{i}$
Hence $\alpha^{8}=\beta^{8}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\left|\alpha^{8}+\beta^{8}\right|=\left|2 \alpha^{8}\right|=2\left|\alpha^{2}\right|^{4} \\
=2 \sqrt{5}^{4}=50

Sol. $\mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q} \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \sim(p \vee q) \vee q \\
\Rightarrow(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee q \\
\Rightarrow(\sim p \vee q) \wedge(\sim q \vee q) \\
\Rightarrow(\sim p \vee q) \wedge t=\sim p \vee q

Now by taking option C
$$\begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow \sim \mathrm{p} \vee \sim \mathrm{q} \vee \sim \mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q} \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{t}

Hence C

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\left[\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}\right]$ be a square matrix of order 3 such that $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{ij}}=2^{\mathrm{j}-\mathrm{i}}$, for all $\mathrm{i}, \mathrm{j}=1,2,3$. Then, the matrix $\mathrm{A}^{2}+\mathrm{A}^{3}+\ldots+\mathrm{A}^{10}$ is equal to :

options.D:
$\left(\frac{3^{10}+3}{2}\right) A$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)

Sol. $\quad \mathrm{A}=\left(\begin{array}{lll}1 & 2 & 2^{2} \\ 1 / 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 / 2^{2} & 1 / 2 & 1\end{array}\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
A^{2}=3 A \\
A^{3}=3^{2} A \\
A^{2}+A^{3}+\ldots . A^{10} \\
=3 A+3^{2} A+\ldots+3^{9} A=\frac{3\left(3^{9}-1\right)}{3-1} A \\
=\frac{3^{10}-3}{2} A
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Let $\left\{a_{n}\right\}_{n=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence such that $\mathrm{a}_{0}=\mathrm{a}_{1}=0$ and $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}+2}=2 \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}+1}-\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}+1$ for all $n \geq 0$. Then, $\sum_{\mathrm{n}=2}^{\infty} \frac{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{n}}}{7^{\mathrm{n}}}$ is equal to

options.D:
$\frac{49}{216}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)

JEE Exam Solution
www.esaral.com
3

Saral
JEE | NEET | Class 8-10 Download eSaral APP

Sol. $\mathrm{a}_{2}=1, \mathrm{a}_{3}=3 \mathrm{a}_{4}=6$
$$\begin{array}{l}
a_{n}=\frac{n(n-1)}{2} \\
S=\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{n(n-1)}{2\left(7^{n}\right)} \\
S=\frac{1}{7^{2}}+\frac{3}{7^{3}}+\frac{6}{7^{4}}+\frac{10}{7^{5}}+\frac{15}{7^{5}}+\ldots \ldots \\
\frac{S}{7}=\frac{1}{7^{3}}+\frac{3}{7^{4}}+\frac{6}{7^{5}}+\frac{10}{7^{6}}+\ldots \\
6 \frac{S}{7}=\frac{1}{7^{2}}+\frac{2}{7^{3}}+\frac{3}{7^{4}}+\frac{4}{7^{5}}+\ldots \\
6 \frac{S}{7^{2}}=\frac{1}{7^{3}}+\frac{2}{7^{4}}+\frac{3}{7^{5}}+\ldots \\
6 \frac{S}{7} \cdot \frac{6}{7}=\frac{1}{7^{2}}+\frac{1}{7^{3}}+\ldots=\frac{1 / 7^{2}}{1-1 / 7} \\
6 \times 6 \frac{S}{7^{2}}=\cdot \frac{1}{7 \times 6} \\
S=\frac{7}{6^{3}}=\frac{7}{216}
\end{array}$$

Alternate
$$\begin{array}{l}
a_{n+2}=2 a_{n+1}-a_{n}+1 \\
\Rightarrow \frac{a_{n+2}}{7^{n+2}}=\frac{2}{7} \frac{a_{n+1}}{7^{n+1}}-\frac{1}{49} \frac{a_{n}}{7^{n}}+\frac{1}{7^{n+2}} \\
\Rightarrow \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{a_{n+2}}{7^{n+2}}=\frac{2}{7} \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{a_{n+1}}{7^{n+1}}-\frac{1}{49} \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{a_{n}}{7^{n}}+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{7^{n+2}} \\
\text { Let } \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{a_{n}}{7^{n}}=p \\
\Rightarrow\left(p-\frac{a_{2}}{7^{2}}-\frac{a_{3}}{7^{3}}\right)=\frac{2}{7}\left(p-\frac{a_{2}}{7^{2}}\right)-\frac{1}{49} p+\frac{1 / 7^{4}}{1-\frac{1}{7}} \\
\because a_{2}=1, a_{3}=3 \\
\Rightarrow p-\frac{1}{49}-\frac{3}{343}=\frac{2}{7} p-\frac{2}{7^{3}}-\frac{p}{49}+\frac{1}{6.7^{3}} \\
\Rightarrow p=\frac{7}{216}
\end{array}$$

$$\begin{array}{l}

a=2 / 13 \\
A_{T}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} a^{2}+b^{2} \\
=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} x^{2} / 9+\frac{(22-x)^{2}}{16} \\

questions.text: Let PQ be a focal chord of the parabola $y^{2}=4 x$ such that it subtends an angle of $\frac{\pi}{2}$ at the point (3, $0)$. Let the line segment PQ be also a focal chord of the ellipse $\mathrm{E}: \frac{\mathrm{x}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}+\frac{\mathrm{y}^{2}}{\mathrm{~b}^{2}}=1, \mathrm{a}^{2}>\mathrm{b}^{2}$. If e is the eccentricity of the ellipse E, then the value of $\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^{2}}$ is equal to :

options.D:
$4+5 \sqrt{3}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. PQ is focal chord
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{PR}} \cdot \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{PQ}}=-1 \\
\frac{2 \mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{t}^{2}-3} \times \frac{-2 / \mathrm{t}}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{t}^{2}}-3}=-1 \\
\left(\mathrm{t}^{2}-1\right)^{2}=0 \\
\Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=1
\end{array}$$

⇒ P \& Q must be end point of latus rectum:
$$\mathrm{P}(1,2) \& \mathrm{Q}(1,-2)$$
$\therefore \frac{2 \mathrm{~b}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}}=4 \& \mathrm{ae}=1$
∵ We know that $\mathrm{b}^{2}=\mathrm{a}^{2}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{2}\right)$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\therefore \mathrm{a}=1+\sqrt{2} \\
\because \mathrm{e}^{2}=1-\frac{\mathrm{b}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}} \\
\therefore \mathrm{e}^{2}=3-2 \sqrt{2} \\
\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}^{2}}=3+2 \sqrt{2}
\end{array}$$
